packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 18 - BLIND IMAGE READING (unverified)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. I did not open packet.json or any other file beyond PROMPT.md and the eight images. I did run `ls` on the packet directory (to get filenames/sizes) and made enhanced copies (autocontrast + contrast boost, 2x enlargement) in work/zoom18/: a_red_top, a_02b, a_02c, a_04top, a_04mid, a_04bottom, b_06top, b_06red, b_07red1, b_07red2, b_07black, b_08a, b_08b. (a_02c was generated but not viewed.) All eight packet images loaded.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Object: a long, narrow vertical parchment strip (approx. 3-3.5 cm wide judging by the ruler, ca. 25 cm long), photographed on both faces. image-001 = overview of face A (shelf-type mark "F 7370" written in pencil/white near top); image-002/003/004 = tiles of face A top/middle/bottom. image-005 = overview of face B; image-006/007/008 = tiles of face B top/middle/bottom. Tiles overlap (e.g. top of 003 repeats the bottom of 002; top of 008 repeats the bottom of 007); I did not count repeated lines twice.
- A vertical fold/crack runs down the strip about one quarter from the left edge on A (and correspondingly right on B); a horizontal crease/stain band crosses the middle. Much of the middle of both faces is darkened, abraded and crumpled; text there is largely illegible.
- Single column of text only; the strip is a vertical cut through a written column, so line beginnings and line ends are both lost (every line is cut on both sides). No margins, running titles, glosses or initials are visible within the strip. Gothic textualis book hand, heavily abbreviated.
- Ink colour: blocks of text are written entirely in red and other blocks in brown/black, alternating (A: red block of 6 lines at top, dark block below, a reddish band mid-strip, dark lines, then one red line at bottom; B: dark lines at top, red block of 3 lines, dark block, red block of 4 lines, dark block, long red block of ~20+ lines to the bottom). Interpretation (tentative only): red blocks may be one text layer (e.g. a text or rubricated passages) and black another (e.g. commentary), or simply colour alternation; I cannot determine which from this strip.
- On face B top (image-006) the right portion of each line is very faint/pinkish, possibly show-through or offset rather than written text on this face; the left part is crisp black.
- Final line on A (image-004) is red after a black line ending with a period; it looks like a heading/rubric line opening a new section, followed by blank parchment (bottom margin).

SELECTED SPANS: A top red block (002), A bottom lines + red final line (004); B top black lines (006), B red block (006), B red blocks (007, 008). Middle dark zones of both faces (002 lower half, 003 almost entirely, 007 middle) remain essentially unread.

Conventions: line numbers are counted from the first text line in each image; "-" at line start/end = cut by the strip edge; (..) = proposed expansion; ? = uncertain; [illegible].

=== FACE A ===

002.7-10 (dark/brown, mostly illegible): 002.10 ends "...ca(us)a? ..."; one line reads "...es ...ex...s(ec)ondi? i(n)testinu(m)? ca(us)a? ..." [very uncertain]; next "...cu(m) ...ch .i. ... p(ro)p(ri)? ... "; next "...-iores ... ex ... s(ecundu)m? ... " - all [largely illegible]
002 rest and image-003: [illegible] except scattered letters; a line in 003 (~y 560) shows "...sp(eci)alis? ... i(n)fl(amm)ationem? ..." [very uncertain]; 003 near bottom: "... -i? ... ex? solu(m)? ... i(n)forma(n)? ..." [uncertain]

Note: the phrase read "i(n)fallacia" (or similar) occurs in the last red line on both faces (002.6 on A, 008.19 on B). I report it as seen; I cannot say whether these are the same word or a misreading on my part.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is cropped at both ends (strip is only a narrow vertical section of a column); no line is complete.
- The central portion of both faces is darkened, crumpled and abraded; text there is mostly unreadable even with contrast enhancement.
- Much of what I give for black-ink lines is low confidence; red lines on A top (002) and B bottom (007-008) are the most reliable but still heavily abbreviated and partly uncertain.
- I cannot tell which face is recto/verso, nor whether the faint right-hand text on 006 is written text or show-through.
- Suggested follow-up: multispectral or UV imaging of the middle zones; raking light for the crumpled area; if any other strips from the same leaf exist, adjacent strips would supply line beginnings/ends.
